topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Fundamentals of cancer etiology and mutation origins
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous, inherited, and environmental sources of DNA mutations.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and epidemiological risk patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine known environmental exposures, public understanding of cancer causation, and geographic variations in cancer incidence revealed by epidemiological studies.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and viral carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote cancer, highlighted by the detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma pathogenesis.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to form DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, tissue susceptibility, and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic tumor promotion, developmental and tissue susceptibility to carcinogenesis, and summarise the mechanisms of DNA damage.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and assessing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review mutational signature analysis, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo toxicological models, and in vitro Ames testing used to assess carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing remarks, summarising the lecture and framing everyday risk-benefit choices surrounding carcinogen exposure.
